seo_title: Cost of Living in Barcelona 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Barcelona per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The cosmopolitan capital of Catalonia, with the sea, an IT scene and well-developed infrastructure for nomads. More expensive than Valencia, but it offers more opportunities for work and cultural life.
pros: The sea and the Barceloneta and Bogatell beaches within the city
A strong IT industry and startup scene (22@)
A digital nomad visa with a 24% tax rate
Well-developed international infrastructure for families with children
Proximity to the Pyrenees and the French Riviera
cons: High rental costs and a tourist season that lasts all year
Complex bureaucracy around the NIE and empadronamiento
Catalan is mandatory in public services and schools
Pickpocketing in the centre — the highest in Europe

best_places.name: Gràcia

visa_steps.title: Schengen visa or residence permit
visa_steps.description: For long stays — a national D visa through the consulate.

visa_steps.title: Digital Nomad Visa
visa_steps.description: For remote workers earning from €2,763 a month. A residence permit for 1 year, extendable up to 5 years.

visa_steps.title: NIE and TIE
visa_steps.description: An identification number and a physical resident card. Apply through the consulate or the extranjería office.

visa_steps.title: Empadronamiento
visa_steps.description: Address registration at the Ayuntamiento. Without it you can't arrange schooling, healthcare or a phone contract.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: BBVA, CaixaBank, Sabadell. For digital nomads, N26 or Revolut works well to start with.

faq.question: How does Barcelona differ from Valencia?
faq.answer: Barcelona is bigger, more expensive and more dynamic: the IT scene is stronger, but the cost of living is 30–40% higher.

faq.question: Which language should I learn in Barcelona?
faq.answer: Spanish is essential. Catalan — for school and public services. English is used in the IT industry and tourism.

faq.question: Where should I live in Barcelona?
faq.answer: Eixample — central and pricey. Poblenou — a trendy IT district by the sea. Gràcia — quiet and Catalan. Sarrià — premium for families.

faq.question: What about schools for children in Barcelona?
faq.answer: International schools (Benjamin Franklin, BFIS, Kensington) — from €12,000 a year. Public schools are in Catalan.

faq.question: How safe is Barcelona?
faq.answer: The city is safe in terms of violent crime, but pickpocketing is the highest in Europe — especially on La Rambla and in the metro.

faq.question: How is healthcare in Barcelona?
faq.answer: Public care through residency, private clinics (Quironsalud, Teknon) — at EU level.

reviews.text: I got the DNV and rent an apartment in Poblenou for €1,800. The sea is 10 minutes away and I work for an American startup. The downsides — pickpockets in the metro and the noise of tourists.
I'm learning Catalan for my daughter's school. Barcelona is expensive, but the balance of work, the sea and cultural life is the best I've found in Europe.
